metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Factsheets – United Arab Emirates

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for the United Arab Emirates using OECD’s published PISA 2022 database tables (e.g., I.B1.* and II.B1.*). The note does not describe the microdata extraction or any analyst-applied sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures, so weight usage cannot be confirmed from the text. For users working with PISA microdata, analyses should apply the official PISA student sampling weights and replicate weights (as provided in the PISA database) to obtain correct standard errors under the complex two-stage sampling design (students nested in schools). The factsheet also reports uncertainty via 95% confidence intervals, consistent with complex-survey variance estimation, but the specific weight variable names are not provided here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable because this document is a descriptive results factsheet that reports OECD-published estimates (means, proficiency shares, and trend comparisons) rather than training predictive models on student-level PV outcomes. Missing-data handling is not reported because the factsheet does not provide the underlying microdata processing steps (e.g., PV estimation procedure or missing questionnaire/test responses) and instead relies on OECD’s already-produced database tables. Therefore, the appropriate PV/missing-data methodology is embedded in the OECD PISA database production pipeline, not documented in this factsheet.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports the United Arab Emirates analytic participation for PISA 2022: 24,600 students in 840 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, representing about 60,800 15-year-olds (an estimated 94% of the total population of 15-year-olds). No additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., grade restrictions beyond the 15-year-old target, subject-booklet assignment rules, or missing-response exclusions) are specified in the factsheet text; it therefore reflects the OECD’s standard PISA sampling and participation processing for the country.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet summarizes performance and equity-related patterns for 15-year-old students in the United Arab Emirates across mathematics, reading, and science. It reports descriptive benchmarks such as mean scores, proficiency levels (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and trend comparisons with earlier PISA cycles (notably 2018 and 2012), using OECD’s published PISA 2022 database tables. The factsheet also highlights within-country gaps by socio-economic status (ESCS quintiles and top/bottom 25%), gender differences, and immigrant background differences, alongside contextual indicators from student and principal questionnaires (belonging, discipline, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning experiences). Uncertainty is presented via 95% confidence intervals, and the note states that UAE met PISA quality standards for reporting (no asterisk). Because this is not an ML study, no model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/R²) or PV/missing-data procedures are described at the factsheet level; interpretation should focus on policy-relevant descriptive patterns rather than causal claims.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet rather than an empirical ML paper. It does not specify an analytic modeling strategy, target variables, or predictive algorithms, and it does not report an original student-level dataset construction or ML evaluation. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally empty, while the outcome summary focuses on OECD-published descriptive statistics and proficiency/inequality indicators.
